title: Service Credit Terms of the Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
## The basis

Where catering under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement arrives late or falls short of what was ordered, the client is credited against the invoice for that order rather than refunded separately.

## How lateness is measured

Lateness is measured from the service start time on the order to the time the team actually began service, and each complete quarter hour late earns the percentage of order value printed against the service level.

## Quality

An upheld food quality complaint earns the quality credit percentage printed against the service level, and where an order is both late and short the two credits are added together rather than the larger being taken alone.

## The ceiling

Credits against one order are held to the ceiling printed against the service level, and a claim worth more than the ceiling is settled at the ceiling and closed rather than carried onto the next order.

## The claim window

A credit is allowed only when the claim reaches Larkspur Table no later than the claim window for the service level, counted in calendar days from the day the order was delivered. Claim window days are counted as calendar days from the day after delivery, every day of the week counts, and a claim arriving on the boundary day itself is still in time; calendar days are never converted into full 24-hour periods. The delivery day is taken from the delivery entry standing in the company's own order history against that order reference, and the window is tested before the credit is allowed.

**Boundary illustration.** On a hypothetical order whose service level carries a claim window of 14 days and which was delivered on the first day of a month, counting begins on the second day of that month; a claim arriving on the fifteenth day of the month falls on the boundary day and is in time, while a claim arriving on the sixteenth day is out of time. Weekends and public holidays inside the window count like any other day.

## Lateness the client caused

Lateness caused by the client — a room that was not free, a security desk that held the team, a delivery address changed on the day — is not a late delivery for this purpose and earns no credit.

## Orders never delivered

A credit is never allowed against an order that was cancelled and never delivered, since no service was given to fall short of.
